messages:
jun: heads up — we've been seeing steady GPU memory growth on the on-prem racks during long-chat load tests. looks like the KV cache isn't reclaiming certain frames when sequence length grows, so the host eventually hits OOM and starts swapping pages back, causing huge tail latency spikes.

alexa: can you paste the profiler output? where does the leak look like — runtime or host driver?

jun: here's the condensed profile from rdw-profiler (shortened):
```
KVCache::total_pages = 214748
KVCache::active_sets = 1300
KVCache::pinned_frames = 20480
page_faults/sec = 12.4
gpu_driver = nvidia-470.161
model_variant = redwood-llama-7b-ql6
hot_path: kv_lookup -> kv_pin_frame -> nnserve_kernel_select
eviction_attempts = 0 (because pin count > 0)
```

jun: note pinned_frames growth correlates with long-context streams (20k+ tokens) from our private deployment tests. Dedicated (cloud) didn't show the same magnitude, probably due to newer drivers and different cgroup/memory limits.

matt: interesting — on Hosted we've got `kv_max_pinned=4096` and an aggressive aging eviction. Dedicated uses `kv_max_pinned=16384` but driver 525. So two factors: config and driver-level page reclaim semantics.

ria: any VPC-specific constraints here? I remember some customers reported MTU and NIC offload causing unexpected huge page allocations during KV sync.

jun: yes, on the VPC/private stack we observed slower DMA bounce buffers and occasional GPU page faults when pages spilled to host. That increases pin durations.

oliver: could it be our kernel selection causing extra KV copies? If the selected kernel doesn't support zero-copy path we end up with extra host roundtrips and pins.

jun: nailed it — profiler shows fallback to the memcpy kernel for certain sequence lengths and model layout combinations. When memcpy is used, we pin the buffer until the whole request finishes which for streaming requests is very long.

alexa: quick mitigation ideas?

matt: short-term: lower `kv_max_pinned` on on-prem, enable `kv_reclaim_aging=true` and enable `kv_force_partial_unpin=true` (experimental) in config. That will let us evict cold frames even if partially pinned. Also ramp kernel selection thresholds to prefer the tiled kernel which supports streaming zero-copy.

ria: long-term we should make kernel selection aware of pin durations and reuse-window heuristics. i.e., if a kernel path causes long pin times, favor more batch-friendly kernels even if they're slightly slower per-token.

jun: repro steps added to the thread:
1) run `rdw-load --model redwood-llama-7b-ql6 --streaming --seq 25k --concurrency 8 --duration 30m` on on-prem node with nv-driver 470.
2) watch `nvidia-smi` and `rdw-profiler kv` every 5m.
3) you'll see `pinned_frames` climb and `page_faults/sec` tick up, then OOM in ~20-40m depending on load.

oliver: i've got a lab node with driver 525 and will run the same to confirm divergence. if driver change helps, we should add a runtime warning during deploy for old drivers.

deploy-bot: alert #eng-runtime — regression detected: kv memory growth > 10% over baseline in test: private-long-context-streaming (run id: run-2026-11-04-08)

alexa: good call on the driver warning. also add a config lint rule so Dedicated vs Private profiles don't drift on `kv_max_pinned` and `kv_reclaim_aging`. config drift is biting us here.

matt: for the product-facing mitigation we can backstop with a circuit-breaker: if `pinned_frames` > threshold for X minutes, reject new streaming sessions with a friendly 503 + retry-after header and a telemetry event. Less p95 pain than full node OOM.

ria: will open a small RFC for: (1) kernel selection telemetry, (2) pin-time-aware eviction policy, (3) config linter + deploy-time driver check.

jun: thanks — i'll drop an internal gist with the full trace and a sample config patch. TL;DR: cause = memcpy fallback + old driver + looser pinned limits in private; fixes = tune kernel thresholds, reclaim policy, driver check, and circuit breaker.

oliver: assigning myself to run driver comparison and verify perf regression on the lab node this week.

matt: i'll add the linter rule and a temporary emergency config to reduce `kv_max_pinned` on all private clusters.

alexa: awesome. mark as follow-up for next runtime retro. :thumbsup:
